data.name: Octaviel
data.long_meaning:
Derived from the Roman numeral octo, meaning 'eight', Octaviel is a name of Latin origin with a connection to the Bible. In the New Testament, the name Octavian is given to a Roman soldier who converts to Christianity after encountering St. Peter and St. Paul.
This name holds a deep spiritual significance, representing the eighth day or the eighth day of creation, a time of new beginnings and renewed faith.
Octaviel is a strong and faithful name, a symbol of courage and wisdom, carrying with it a sense of deep rooted loyalty and compassion.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes new beginnings and renewed faith

in_greek.name: ΟκταβIEL
in_greek.long_meaning: ΟκταβIEL είναι το όνομα που προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη Octavus, που σημαίνει 'ο όγδοος', και το επίθημα el, που έχει εβραϊκή ρίζα και σημαίνει 'Θεός' ή 'άγγελος', υποδηλώνοντας σύνδεση με τη θεότητα, και στην χριστιανική παράδοση αντιπροσωπεύει αγιότητα και θείο έργο

in_latin.name: Octaviel

historical_references.context: Octavian was a Roman soldier who was converted to Christianity at the insistence of his wife, Octavie. They suffered persecution during the reign of Emperor Maximian (late 3rd century). Octavian was martyred, and Octavie, who was pregnant at the time, died by suicide to avoid being forced into prostitution.
